tasks.short: Compile and format useful remote-sensing image data.

steps.what: Choose source scenes and inspect acquisition metadata in the imagery catalogue
Set and check actual coordinate, band, resolution, extent and output-format parameters in GIS
Repeat scene extraction, reprojection, band ordering and image export in GIS
Inspect draft pixels and metadata and check usefulness, alignment and missing-data handling
Save the checked final image package in the project repository

tasks.design: Test native {OTHER} GIS batch processing for the checked image specification before writing a pipeline. It replaces repeated interactive formatting; source selection, parameter judgement and pixel-level checks remain human.
tasks.enabler_now: Native batch processors reuse explicit formatting parameters.
tasks.still_hard: Detecting misregistration and scientifically harmful resampling.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether formatted pixels remain useful for the intended analysis.
tasks.altitude: Less repetitive formatting, unchanged scientific responsibility.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native GIS batch tools can repeat reprojection and image exports from explicit parameters; output validity still needs inspection.

assumptions: Boundary is image compilation and formatting through repository save. Catalogue producer supplies scene ID, acquisition time, coordinate system, band metadata and source URI. Scientist selects actual scenes in s1 and captures target coordinates, resolution, extent, bands and format in s2; invalid metadata or unsupported operations revert to manual formatting.

Native first. Provisional40 share is actual interactive repetition, not computer runtime; existing unattended batch work earns zero saving. All specification capture and scientific checking counted. Save1 fully retained; s4 is ordinary output checking, no extra approval ceremony.
unknowns: Actual interactive repetition and native batch coverage
research_questions: Do native batch outputs retain expected pixel alignment and metadata?

incremental.description: Maintain batch settings and format compatibility

approvals.approved_version: s4 checked final image package and project destination

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Provisional40 interactive formatting units removed minus2 upkeep=38. Half eligible repetitions gives18. Source selection20, parameter capture15, scientific inspection24 and save1 unchanged.

tasks.short: Prepare and deliver geospatial project reports and presentations.

steps.what: Collect actual project datasets, methods, validation results and reporting requirements
Interpret project findings, uncertainty and implications for the actual audience
Populate the report maps, figures and tables from actual selected project outputs
Write report narrative explaining the actual findings and limitations

loop.purpose: Draft explanatory prose from selected findings
loop.input: Checked project evidence pack and scientist-selected findings and limitations
loop.output: Draft project report with evidence links
loop.check: Scientist verifies each claim against actual results, uncertainty and methods; rejects overstated causality, omitted limitations and misleading map interpretations.
loop.stop: Missing evidence or two failed revisions returns prose to manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Native figure templates handle fixed content first; variable explanation of selected findings needs prose composition.

steps.what: Check the complete final report, figures, source versions and intended recipients
Send the checked final geospatial report to its authorised project recipients
Present actual project findings and answer audience questions

tasks.design: Configure native {OTHER} GIS report layouts and {DOCS} templates first for actual figures and tables. A bounded drafting loop may explain scientist-selected findings; the scientist checks the full final report before send and delivers the presentation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated figure insertion and narrative drafting.
tasks.enabler_now: Native report layouts and evidence-bounded text drafting.
tasks.still_hard: Representing geospatial uncertainty and avoiding misleading conclusions.
tasks.human_edge: Select defensible findings and answer methodological challenges.
tasks.altitude: Less report assembly; no scientific decision rights gained.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: GIS report templates assemble selected outputs and a bounded text draft can explain supplied findings, subject to scientific verification.

assumptions: Boundary covers report preparation, send and presentation. Project producers supply dataset IDs, versions, units, maps, methods and actual validation results; scientist checks these in s1 and selects findings in s2. Missing evidence is manually assembled; no unverified automatic extraction.

Native first; existing automatic figure refresh earns zero. Shares are provisional activity mix, not measured. Model and final checks are counted in s4-s5. Final QA is existing report work, not added ceremony. Send1 fully retained.
unknowns: Actual report assembly effort and permitted model access
research_questions: Can drafted prose preserve uncertainty and correct spatial interpretation?

incremental.description: Maintain report mappings and audit narrative samples

approvals.approved_version: s5 checked complete final geospatial report and authorised recipients

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Provisional figure assembly15 removed plus narrative19 reduced40 percent saves7.6; gross22.6 minus2 upkeep=20.6. Half eligible report assembly and prose gives9.3. Findings, evidence checks, final QA, send and presentation unchanged.

tasks.short: Discuss project goals, equipment and methodologies with colleagues.

steps.what: Find actual project goals, equipment specifications and current method papers
Discuss actual project goals, equipment requirements and methodological choices with colleagues
outputs: actual agreed goals and method decisions

steps.what: Write and check actual agreed requirements and method decisions in the project notes
inputs: actual agreed goals and method decisions

steps.what: Save the checked project decision note

tasks.design: Use a native {DOCS} project folder with links to current requirements and method papers. Keep actual methodological discussion and ordinary decision-note writing human.
tasks.enabler_now: Native folders and pinned source links.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge assumptions and resolve scientific tradeoffs.
tasks.altitude: Less source hunting; collaborative decisions unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: linked native project documents reduce repeated source finding without replacing methodological discussion.

assumptions: Boundary is actual project discussion and its actual method-decision note, not secretariat minutes. Project authors supply goal text, equipment revision and method source links. Scientist verifies sources in s1 and writes actual decisions in s3; missing links require manual search.
Native first. Existing links earn zero. Provisional shares; no measured baseline. Normal note checking stays in writing, no added approval meeting. Save1 fully retained.
unknowns: Actual source finding and note requirements
research_questions: Are current project source links already sufficient?

tasks.short: Process aerial or satellite imagery into land-cover products.

steps.what: Choose suitable aerial or satellite scenes and check actual metadata and coverage
Produce and check actual training labels and independent reference samples
Set and check preprocessing, classification and output parameters in GIS
Repeat interactive preprocessing, selected classification execution and map export across scenes
Inspect map outputs and test actual class errors against independent reference samples
outputs: checked map and actual validation findings

steps.what: Write and check actual processing provenance, validation results and limitations for the final map
inputs: checked map and actual validation findings
outputs: checked final map package with provenance

steps.what: Save the checked final map package and provenance in the project repository
inputs: checked final map package with provenance

tasks.design: Use native {OTHER} GIS processing models to rerun the scientist-selected preprocessing and classification operations. Preserve actual training capture, parameter decisions, independent validation and final provenance; only repeated interactive execution changes.
tasks.enabler_now: Native reusable processing models; code only for unsupported operators.
tasks.still_hard: Cloud contamination, reference quality and transfer between places or seasons.
tasks.human_edge: Judge class meaning and whether validation supports the intended use.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated processing setup; scientific decisions unchanged.

evidence.claim: Copernicus openEO supports rerunnable scripts over Sentinel datacubes; this supports repeatable processing, not automatic scientific validity.
Model knowledge: native GIS processing models can repeat selected operations while scientists retain training and validation work.

assumptions: Boundary is actual land-cover product processing through final save. Catalogue supplies scene IDs, timestamps, bands and coordinates; scientist captures labels and independent samples in s2 and actual algorithm, masks, resolution, class scheme and output parameters in s3. Unsupported or missing inputs revert to manual processing; no free extraction.

Native configuration first. Provisional25 share is human interactive repetition, never unattended compute runtime. Already scripted work earns zero. Actual training20, parameter decisions10, validation20 and provenance4 remain counted. Save1 fully retained.
unknowns: Existing automation and native operator coverage
research_questions: Which interactive processing repetitions remain after native configuration?
